name.text: Determining the Length of a Divider Arm from Vertical Height

questiontext.text:
The angle formed by the arms of an upright pair of dividers and the horizontal is \({@theta@}^\circ\). The vertical distance from the horizontal to the vertex is \({@d@}\,\text{cm}\). Find the length of one arm of the divider without using a calculator or trigonometric tables.

[[jsxgraph]] /* Fetch the randomized variables from STACK */ var theta_deg = {#theta#}; var height_val = {#d#}; /* Convert angle to radians for JavaScript math */ var theta_rad = theta_deg * Math.PI / 180; /* Lock the visual height and calculate the base width */ var h = 5; var w = h / Math.tan(theta_rad); var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-(w + 1.5), h + 1.5, w + 1.5, -1.0], axis: false, keepaspectratio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); /* Define the key points */ var O = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: '', visible: false, fixed: true}); var L = board.create('point', [-w, 0], {name: '', visible: false, fixed: true}); /* Left needle tip */ var R = board.create('point', [w, 0], {name: '', visible: false, fixed: true}); /* Right needle tip */ /* Calculate where the thick arms should end and the thin needles should begin (15% from the bottom) */ var L_arm_end = board.create('point', [-w * 0.85, h * 0.15], {visible: false, fixed: true}); var R_arm_end = board.create('point', [w * 0.85, h * 0.15], {visible: false, fixed: true}); /* The Hinge (Vertex) - Drawn as a visible circular joint */ var V = board.create('point', [0, h], { name: '', visible: true, size: 6, face: 'circle', fillColor: '#b0b5b9', strokeColor: '#333333', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true }); /* Draw the horizontal surface line */ board.create('segment', [[-(w + 1.5), 0], [w + 1.5, 0]], {strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); /* Draw the thick metallic divider arms */ board.create('segment', [V, L_arm_end], {strokeColor: '#88929E', strokeWidth: 9, lineCap: 'round', fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [V, R_arm_end], {strokeColor: '#88929E', strokeWidth: 9, lineCap: 'round', fixed: true}); /* Draw the sharp needles at the ends */ board.create('segment', [L_arm_end, L], {strokeColor: '#333333', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [R_arm_end, R], {strokeColor: '#333333', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true}); /* Draw the vertical height (dashed) */ board.create('segment', [V, O], {strokeColor: '#e74c3c', dash: 2, strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); /* Add the right-angle mark at the origin */ board.create('angle', [R, O, V], {radius: 0.4, type: 'square', name: ''}); /* Add the angle theta at the right foot (with a slight yellow fill to match your original) */ board.create('angle', [V, R, O], { radius: 1.0, name: theta_deg + '°', fontSize: 14, fillColor: '#f1c40f', fillOpacity: 0.3 }); /* Label the vertical height */ board.create('text', [0.2, h / 2, height_val + ' cm'], {anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle', fixed: true, fontSize: 14}); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

We are asked to find the length of one arm of the divider given:

  • Angle with the horizontal: \({@theta@}^\circ\)
  • Vertical distance from the horizontal to the vertex: \({@d@} \text{ cm}\)

From trigonometry, the vertical height acts as the opposite side, and the arm acts as the hypotenuse. Therefore, the relationship is:

\(\begin{align} \text{Arm length} &= \frac{\text{Vertical distance}}{\sin \theta} \\ &= \frac{{@d@}}{\sin({@theta@}^\circ)} \\ &= \frac{{@d@}}{{@sin(theta*pi/180)@}} \\ &= {@arm_length@} \text{ cm} \end{align}\)

Hence, the exact length of one arm of the divider is \({@arm_length@} \text{ cm}\).
